chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, raising it, said:
The sanctuary of the river is its banks and what is adjacent to them.

key_terms.حَرِيمُ: Sanctuary or protected zone; an area where certain rights are restricted or protected.
key_terms.يَلِيهَا: What is adjacent to or next to it.

ai.seo_question: What is the legal definition of a river's sanctuary (haram) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this concise hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the legal boundary of a river's sanctity, defining the banks and adjacent land as integral to the water body's protected zone. This ruling is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for resolving disputes over public rights, grazing, and construction, ensuring that the natural ecosystem remains inviolable. It reflects the broader Islamic principle of preserving natural resources as a trust (amanah) for the community.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, raising it,
‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Sanctuary of the river is its bank and what is adjacent to it’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father in a marfu’ manner the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said,
the restricted area around a canal is up to its edge and that which adjoins it.”
